# Guardian Consent and Participation Form

SmartBridge FET | TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd
Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

Operator: TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd, CIPC registration 2026/155090/07. Registered office: 6 Marais Road, Stellenbosch, Western Cape, 7600, South Africa. Support: aneleq@techandguard.co.za. SmartBridge FET is the platform brand; no registered trademark status is claimed.

## Purpose
Record the learner's participation and the competent person's authority where required. A staff member must verify the request before enabling any account/report access. Do not collect national identity numbers, health details or banking information on this form.

## Choices
Permission for learning-platform participation does not automatically permit public learner photographs, session recordings, direct marketing, sensitive-data AI processing or disclosure to unrelated tutors/parents. Separate, specific consent is needed where applicable. Learner-approved report links remain subject to lawful guardian-authority review.

## Declaration
I have reviewed the service and parent/student terms and understand the fee/cancellation policy. I will contact support if authority, consent or the learner's circumstances change. I understand withdrawal or a deletion request may require identity/authority verification and lawful record-retention review. Complete and retain this form. Submit only through a private channel arranged with support. Consent takes effect only after the competent person's authority has been checked.

## Information covered by core participation consent
Core participation involves the learner's account/contact details, grade/subjects, learning activity, bookings, authorised lesson communications, progress, consent and safety records. These support learning, account administration, appropriate parent reporting and protection. The main Privacy Notice explains necessary recipients/providers, overseas processing, retention and your rights. Only necessary information may be collected. Ask support about anything unclear before signing.

## Separate choices — complete each independently
Blank, ambiguous or unselected optional choices mean no permission. Do not bundle optional permission into core participation. This form does not grant any permission for public learner media, recording, marketing or identifying/sensitive AI processing; those require their own purpose-specific process.

- I am legally competent and authorised to consent for this learner: Yes / No.
- I have read the relevant privacy notice and authorise core participation and the described necessary processing: Yes / No.
- I request a parent account link for permitted progress reports, subject to verification: Yes / No.
- Public photographs, learner testimonials and marketing media: NOT authorised by this form.
- Lesson/audio/video recordings: NOT authorised by this form.
- Optional direct marketing: NOT authorised by this form.
- Identifying or sensitive information in AI tools: NOT authorised by this form.

## Withdrawal and verification
You can contact support to withdraw a consent, change a choice, challenge a relationship or exercise applicable privacy rights. Withdrawal may prevent the dependent feature; it does not reverse lawful earlier processing or erase records that must lawfully be retained. A request to link a parent account is not approved solely because this form was signed. Staff must verify authority and record the purpose/version/choices before relying on consent. If authority cannot be established, do not enable child-data processing based on this form.

## Completion and record fields
This is a blank template. Do not enter details into a shared/public copy. Ordinary website acceptance is not a completed signature or proof that identity/authority has been verified.

- Participant full name: ____________________
- Registered account email or account reference: ____________________
- Role and, where relevant, learner account reference: ____________________
- Signatory's capacity/authority: ____________________
- Version read: 2.0
- Signature or attributable electronic signature: ____________________
- Date and place: ____________________
- Competent person's name/signature/date, where required for a minor: ____________________
- Administrator verification date and restricted record reference: ____________________

Allow time to read, ask questions and retain a copy. A witness is optional unless required for a particular document by applicable law; a witness does not establish guardianship.

# Privacy Policy - Parent Addendum

SmartBridge FET | TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd
Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

## Scope
Read this with the Privacy Notice — Learners and All Users, available in the legal library. TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd operates SmartBridge FET and determines how platform personal information is used. Existing company records identify registration 2026/155090/07 and office 6 Marais Road, Stellenbosch, Western Cape, 7600, South Africa. Contact: [aneleq@techandguard.co.za](mailto:aneleq@techandguard.co.za). Address privacy correspondence to the Information Officer through that contact.

## Parent information and authority
We use your account/contact information, your stated relationship to a learner, consent decisions and verification records to manage authorised participation and progress access. We may receive relationship details from the learner or the person requesting a link. We must check contested or unclear authority before disclosing learner information. Being a parent, knowing a learner's email or possessing a completed form does not automatically unlock the learner's account.

## Information you may see
A permitted parent link provides the progress/report information authorised for that relationship. It does not give access to passwords, every private conversation, unrelated learners or tutor credentials. Access for an adult learner requires their permission or another lawful basis. A child's views, safety and applicable legal rights must be considered when handling a guardian request.

## Specific consent
Core participation, public photographs/testimonials, recording, direct marketing and optional AI processing are different purposes. Core guardian consent does not authorise all of them. Optional permissions must identify the purpose, information, recipients and withdrawal route and must remain unselected unless expressly chosen. If no optional permission is recorded, treat it as refused. Do not send another person's data without authority.

## Withdrawal and disputes
Ask support to change consent, correct a relationship, challenge access or request deletion. We will check authority using a proportionate private process and explain the effect on services and any lawful retention. Where guardians disagree or a safety concern exists, access may be restricted while the facts are reviewed. Do not put family-court orders, identity documents or completed consent forms into shared study rooms.

## Records and complaints
Store a copy of the version and choices you sign. Completed forms must be restricted to authorised staff and the relevant account owner, with necessary lawful disclosure only. For the general retention, providers, international transfers, security and regulator complaint route, see the main Privacy Notice. Reading this addendum is not proof that guardian verification has occurred.

title: Service, Media and AI Privacy Addendum
content:
# Service, Media and AI Privacy Addendum

SmartBridge FET | TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd
Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

## Relationship to the privacy notice
This addendum supplements the Privacy Notice — Learners and All Users. Support and privacy requests: [aneleq@techandguard.co.za](mailto:aneleq@techandguard.co.za).

## Service providers and information flows
Supabase provides account, database and storage infrastructure; AWS Amplify hosts the web app. Enabled email services handle necessary recipients and message content. Payment processing, when available, uses the provider identified at checkout. Access must be limited to each provider's function and subject to appropriate contractual/security safeguards. Provider regions and subprocessors may involve international transfers; we must establish a lawful basis and appropriate protections before sharing. These documents do not certify that all vendor or security reviews have been completed.

## AI assistance
Configured AI functions send learning requests to the OpenAI API and return supplementary educational answers or structured study/lesson plans. Availability depends on configuration. Outputs can be wrong, biased or unsuitable; they are not official marks, professional advice or admission decisions. Check important answers with a teacher or reliable source.

Use anonymised academic questions. Do not include names, learner identifiers, ID documents, guardian forms, contact details, health/criminal information or financial details. A general platform acceptance does not authorise children's personal information or special personal information to be sent to an AI service. Where such processing is proposed, it requires a separate lawful assessment, notice, safeguards and consent where required before activation. The API request disables optional response storage in the current code, but that does not guarantee zero provider logging, zero retention or a particular training practice. Support can provide the applicable provider terms for an enabled feature.

## Media and recording
Tutor introduction media is deliberately public when published. A tutor must own it or have permission for all people/materials shown. Learners' images, voices or testimonials must not appear in public marketing without specific valid permission and competent-person consent where required. The default is no recording of a lesson or private chat. Any exception requires an identified purpose, participants, access limits, retention period and separate informed permissions, including a competent person's permission for a child where required. Refusal of optional marketing/media permission must not prevent unrelated core learning access.

## Retention, incidents and requests
Use the main Privacy Notice for rights, retention principles and complaints. Report unintended AI submission or media disclosure privately with a reference; do not repeat sensitive data in a public report. We must assess deletion/containment options with the provider and meet applicable incident-notification duties. A browser deletion alone cannot erase copies already transmitted to a provider.

title: Privacy Notice — Learners and All Users
content:
# Privacy Notice — Learners and All Users

SmartBridge FET | TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd
Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

## 1. Who this notice covers
TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd operates SmartBridge FET and determines how platform personal information is used. Existing company records identify registration 2026/155090/07 and office 6 Marais Road, Stellenbosch, Western Cape, 7600, South Africa. Contact: [aneleq@techandguard.co.za](mailto:aneleq@techandguard.co.za). Address privacy correspondence to the Information Officer through that contact.

This notice covers website visitors, Grades 10–12 learners and registered users. The parent and tutor addenda explain additional uses of their information. Reading a notice or clicking a general acceptance button does not authorise every optional use of your data.

## 2. Information and purposes
Depending on the features you use, the platform receives:
- Account and contact information, login identifiers, account role and security records to register you, authenticate access, prevent misuse and contact you about your account.
- Grade, subjects, learning activity, quiz answers, study plans, attendance and progress to provide educational tools and progress reports.
- Tutor applications, qualifications and verification records to assess applications and manage suitable access.
- Booking details, messages, cancellation reasons, payment references and transaction status to organise lessons, address disputes and keep transaction records. Never send passwords, PINs or full card details to support.
- Guardian relationships, consent records and limited supporting evidence to check authority and decide what information may be shared.
- Content you submit, support requests, incident reports and relevant technical logs to provide features, protect users and investigate problems.

Required information is identified in the relevant form. Without essential account, booking or lawful guardian-authority information, we may be unable to provide that feature. Optional media or marketing permission must not be made a condition of unrelated learning access.

## 3. Why processing is permitted
We assess the appropriate legal basis for each purpose, including providing an agreed service, meeting legal duties, protecting legitimate interests where lawful, and specific consent where needed. For a child's information, a separate lawful authorisation under POPIA's child-information rules is required; ordinary adult contractual or legitimate-interest grounds alone do not bypass those rules. Our standard participation process requires prior informed consent from a competent person whose authority can be verified.

## 4. Who can receive information
Authorised staff and service providers receive information needed for their tasks. Assigned tutors receive the lesson information necessary to teach; linked parents receive permitted learner progress information. Neither group has unrestricted access to a learner's private account. A disputed relationship must be reviewed before disclosure. Providers include Supabase for account/database/storage services and AWS Amplify for website hosting; email and enabled AI services may receive the information necessary for those functions. Payment processing follows the provider identified at checkout. This notice does not mean payments are currently enabled.

Content posted in shared study spaces is visible to their permitted participants. Public tutor profiles and introduction media can be seen publicly. Private credentials, completed agreements, learner identity documents and bank details must never be posted there. Information may also be disclosed where lawfully required by a court, regulator or protective reporting obligation. We do not authorise selling children's personal information or using it for unrelated advertising.

## 5. International processing and AI
SmartBridge FET's database project is configured in Supabase's eu-west-1 region. Hosting, delivery, support and enabled AI processing can involve other countries; the database region does not establish that every copy stays there. Transfers require an appropriate lawful basis and safeguards under POPIA. Contact us for applicable provider details. AI features use the configured OpenAI API when available. Do not enter names, identity numbers, contact details, confidential forms, health information or payment information in prompts. Provider logging and retention can still apply; we do not promise zero retention. The Service, Media and AI Privacy Addendum gives more detail.

## 6. Retention and security
We keep information only while necessary for its recorded purpose or another lawful retention basis, such as transaction evidence, tax duties, dispute resolution or security. Closure of an account does not automatically require destruction of records the law requires us to retain. Retained information must be limited to that purpose, access restricted and erased or de-identified when no longer justified. Backup copies may expire through provider backup cycles rather than disappear instantly. Ask support for the applicable category and retention basis; a subscription is not permission for indefinite retention.

Access permissions, private document storage and versioned consent records support privacy. No online service can guarantee absolute security. Report suspected exposure promptly without reposting leaked information. We will investigate, contain incidents and make the notifications required by law; no contractual clause removes those duties.

## 7. Your choices and rights
Contact support to request access, correction, deletion where applicable, an explanation of processing, withdrawal of consent or an objection permitted by law. We may require proportionate identity and guardian-authority checks, using a private route. We will explain any lawful refusal, applicable fee or retained category and available challenge route. Withdrawal does not undo lawful earlier processing and may prevent a feature that depends on that consent. Request human review of significant automated decisions affecting you.

You can complain directly to the [Information Regulator](https://inforegulator.org.za/) without first completing our internal process. This notice does not restrict statutory complaint deadlines or access rights.

## 8. Browser storage and communications
The web app uses browser storage for authentication and preferences and can retain tutor-profile drafts on a device. Sign out on shared devices and avoid saving confidential information there. Browser controls can clear storage but may sign you out or remove drafts. Marketing permissions are separate from necessary account, safety and booking communications. You can object to marketing through support or an available unsubscribe route. This notice does not authorise non-essential tracking or marketing that requires separate consent.

## 9. Changes
Material changes will be explained before taking effect where required. A new purpose requiring consent needs a new choice; changing this notice cannot retrospectively authorise it. Published wording describes obligations and available processes, not an independent certification of POPIA compliance.

title: Subscription and Booking Cancellation Policy
content:
# Subscription and Booking Cancellation Policy

SmartBridge FET | TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd
Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

Operator: TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd, CIPC registration 2026/155090/07. Registered office: 6 Marais Road, Stellenbosch, Western Cape, 7600, South Africa. Support: aneleq@techandguard.co.za. SmartBridge FET is the platform brand; no registered trademark status is claimed.

## Subscription fees
Subscription fees pay for the selected service/access period and contribute to server hosting, database operation, security, maintenance, support and other services that keep the app working. A change-of-mind request after the agreed service has begun is assessed against the service already supplied, the purchase disclosures and applicable law. Access having started does not by itself remove a cooling-off right. Cancellation of renewal stops future charges in line with disclosed renewal terms; it does not automatically reverse an already supplied period. These fees are not an indefinite personal-data-storage fee and do not override privacy/deletion obligations.

## Mandatory rights take precedence
This policy does not exclude applicable cooling-off, fixed-term cancellation, unfair-term, non-supply, defective-service, duplicate/unauthorised-payment or other statutory remedies. Where law requires a refund, the company will honour it. Any early-start consent must be separate, informed and recorded; a general checkbox is not assumed to remove every cooling-off right.

## Tutor booking fees: at least 24 hours' notice
A paid booking cancelled at least 24 hours before its scheduled start is eligible for a full booking-fee refund. The server measures the exact interval using the session's South African time; cancellation exactly 24 hours beforehand qualifies. Submit the in-app cancellation and write a message informing the tutor that you are cancelling, allowing them to rearrange their day. The message and cancellation timestamp are recorded. A queued or failed email does not invalidate an otherwise timely recorded cancellation or make the learner responsible for an email-provider failure.

## Later cancellations, tutor cancellation and non-delivery
For later cancellations and no-shows, any cancellation charge must be fair, disclosed and justified in the circumstances, including notice and reasonable opportunities to rebook. There is no automatic entitlement to keep the entire booking price. No blanket forfeiture is imposed. Death or hospitalisation affecting the booked beneficiary receives the protection required by law. Do not request detailed medical records through public messages; use a secure minimal-evidence review. A tutor/company cancellation or failure to deliver a booked service is referred for full booking-fee refund when payment was received. Unpaid bookings have no money to return.

## Processing and loss prevention
Refund eligibility is not proof of completed repayment. Refund only the amount actually collected, once, against the original payment/booking reference and normally through the original payment method where practicable. Do not refund subscription revenue as if it were a booking payment. Do not mark a booking refunded or release an associated tutor payout until settlement is verified. Keep an audit trail and reconcile chargebacks to avoid duplicate reimbursement. Do not deduct undisclosed penalties or use processing costs to defeat a mandatory full refund. Contact support with your reference; provider timelines and applicable statutory deadlines will be communicated during review.

## Cooling-off and fixed-term rights
Where ECTA section 44 applies to an electronic service transaction, the consumer generally has seven days after concluding the agreement to cancel without reason or penalty, subject to statutory exclusions. Refunds due under that provision must be made within 30 days of cancellation. A service started with the consumer's consent within the cooling-off period can fall within an exception; do not assume that merely logging in or ticking general terms establishes informed early-start consent. Other products and circumstances must be assessed under the applicable rules.

Where CPA section 14 applies to a fixed-term agreement, a consumer may cancel on 20 business days' recorded notice, subject to a reasonable cancellation charge where permitted. Applicable expiry/renewal notices and rights must be honoured. Direct-marketing cooling-off rights may apply under CPA section 16; they do not simply stack on ECTA-covered transactions. If more favourable commercial terms were promised, honour them. These statutory rights do not require permission from a tutor.

## Non-delivery, quality and technical interruption
For a tutor cancellation or wholly undelivered paid lesson, offer a full booking-fee refund; rescheduling is the customer's choice. Where delivery was partial or materially deficient, assess a reasonable remedy, including correction or an appropriate refund, subject to mandatory rights. Do not treat a brief outage as proof that a whole service was supplied or automatically charge a learner for a failure attributable to the platform. Learner-side connectivity problems require a fair review of what happened and any disclosed reasonable charge.

## Giving notice and following a refund
Use the available cancellation action and a short written notice to the tutor. If the app fails, email support with the booking reference and scheduled date/time. Support must record the notice and consider the evidence of when it was received. A tutor's failure to acknowledge, or a failed system email, does not defeat a valid timely cancellation. The 24-hour promise is a commercial full-refund benefit; later notice does not eliminate statutory protection.

Support will communicate the decision, calculation, original-payment reference, expected processing time and any lawful reason for refusal. Complain if a refund is delayed; provider processing does not excuse a statutory deadline. A full-refund entitlement must not be reduced by an undisclosed platform, administration or payment fee. Credits cannot replace a money refund without your agreement where a money refund is due. Refund only once, taking account of any chargeback already paid.

## Separation from payment activation
This policy governs decisions when money has actually been collected; it does not activate a payment gateway, promise an unverified automated refund process, or authorise a transfer. Until the relevant functionality is working, do not sell a service on the promise that an unavailable payment/refund mechanism exists.

Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

Operator: TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd, CIPC registration 2026/155090/07. Registered office: 6 Marais Road, Stellenbosch, Western Cape, 7600, South Africa. Support: aneleq@techandguard.co.za. SmartBridge FET is the platform brand; no registered trademark status is claimed.

## Authority and learner access
Provide accurate contact details and confirm your authority to act for the learner. Submit evidence only through an approved secure process if requested; do not upload identity documents to public areas. A signed form does not automatically establish guardianship or grant database access. Routine report access follows the approved learner-parent link; questions involving a minor's competent-person consent require review under applicable law.

## Supervision and payment
Help the learner use appropriate equipment, attend agreed sessions and stay safe online. Review the tutor's profile and suitability; platform verification is not a guarantee of outcomes. Read the price, access duration, renewal terms and refund policy before purchasing. Platform subscription fees and tutor booking fees are distinct. Do not share your account or ask a learner to disclose passwords.

## Cancellation and consent
Help the learner submit a written booking cancellation to the tutor. At least 24 hours' notice makes a paid booking eligible for a full booking-fee refund; later notice or exceptional circumstances are reviewed fairly and mandatory rights remain. Subscription refunds follow the shared policy; simply starting access does not automatically remove statutory cooling-off rights. A guardian's permission must be informed and specific; an indemnity does not waive the company's non-excludable duties. Ask support to change consent or seek a verified data-access/deletion process. Retain a copy of the version you accepted and any completed forms.

## Choices, concerns and account closure
Review the main Privacy Notice and Parent Addendum before authorising a child's participation. Core consent does not permit public media, recording or marketing. Use the separate choices on the guardian form and request a private verification route from support. An adult learner controls their own permissions unless another legal authority applies.

Raise concerns about unsuitable contact, misleading tutor credentials or disclosure immediately. Keep relevant messages privately; do not confront a child publicly or distribute allegations. You may request restriction of an unsafe link while authority is reviewed. Closing your account does not automatically close another person's account or delete records needed to protect them.

## Fair responsibility
You are responsible for your own agreement and purchases that you lawfully authorise. These terms do not create unlimited liability for every action of a child or waive a child's rights. Follow the general terms, shared cancellation policy and safeguarding policy. Completed forms are private records, not public profile attachments.

# Terms of Service

## The service
SmartBridge FET provides a learning platform, resources, progress tools and a marketplace for independently provided tutoring. Features offered are those shown as available. We do not guarantee examination results, CAPS certification, school admission, scholarships, employment or uninterrupted internet access. Tutors may not represent themselves as employees or authorised agents unless separately appointed in writing.

## Accounts and young learners
Provide accurate information, protect login details and do not share accounts. Learners under 18 require appropriate parent or guardian authorisation. A parent's relationship and authority must be verified; a downloadable form alone does not grant access to a learner's account. Account privileges and tutor verification are controlled by the company. We may restrict unsafe conduct, fraud, unlawful content or material breaches after fair notice where practicable. Emergency protective suspension may be immediate, with a review channel through support.

## Fees and cancellation
Subscription fees cover the selected access period and contribute to hosting, database operation, security, maintenance, support and third-party services. They are ordinarily non-refundable for change of mind after access starts, subject to mandatory consumer rights and the published refund policy. They are not a charge for indefinite retention of personal information. Cancelling renewal stops future billing according to the disclosed renewal cutoff; it does not erase data or by itself require reimbursement for an already supplied period. Do not charge or renew a plan unless price, duration, renewal terms and consent have been disclosed.

Tutoring booking fees are separate. The Subscription and Booking Cancellation Policy controls eligibility. A refund decision is distinct from actual repayment. No user should be told a refund is completed before payment settlement is confirmed. The company will not collect for unavailable or knowingly undeliverable services.

## Responsible use and content
Do not harass, impersonate, discriminate, cheat, distribute malware, publish illegal or infringing materials, expose personal contact details in public learning areas, or bypass access/payment controls. You retain rights to your original work and permit the platform only to host and display it for the agreed service. Tutors must hold permission for their teaching materials. Public tutor photos and introduction videos are intentionally viewable; do not include identity documents, learners' images without valid consent, banking information or private contact details.

## AI and third-party services
AI is supplementary educational assistance and may be incorrect. Check important answers with an appropriate teacher or source. No automated output is a certification or professional advice. OpenAI integration requires a configured server API project; account registration alone does not activate it. Do not submit sensitive documents, children's identifiers, health details or financial information to AI prompts. Relevant processing and retention must be disclosed in the privacy notice. Third-party outages do not remove statutory service remedies.

## Important risk and liability notice
Online tutoring requires compatible devices, connectivity, responsible behaviour and supervision appropriate to age. Limitations and indemnities apply only to the extent lawful and proportionate. Nothing excludes fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence, mandatory consumer remedies or other liability that cannot legally be excluded. You are responsible for your own unlawful conduct; the company is not automatically responsible for every independent tutor statement. Any claim must be assessed on its facts, with a fair dispute process. We do not promise the company will suffer no losses.

## Complaints, records and changes
Contact support with a booking/payment reference and a description. Do not send passwords or full card details. We will acknowledge complaints and communicate the review route; statutory deadlines take precedence. Preserve acceptance version and transaction records. Material changes apply prospectively after notice and any legally required consent; they do not rewrite a completed transaction. South African law applies without preventing lawful access to courts, regulators or other mandatory remedies.

## Contract formation and document order
You must have an opportunity to read the applicable terms, correct your information and review a purchase before confirming it. A purchase requires the displayed total price, service, supplier, duration and any renewal conditions to be agreed. A general account acceptance does not authorise an undisclosed fee, automatic renewal or recording. For a minor, obtain the required competent-person involvement. Publication alone does not establish an existing user's acceptance of a new contract.

Mandatory law prevails. The shared cancellation/refund policy governs refunds; the relevant learner, parent or tutor terms add role-specific responsibilities. A particular booking or private tutor commercial schedule may add clearly disclosed terms but cannot remove mandatory rights. Any genuine conflict must be resolved fairly and consistently with applicable law. Keep a copy of the version and purchase confirmation.

## Educational and professional claims
SmartBridge FET is supplementary learning support, not a school, examining body or university. CAPS alignment is not government endorsement or accreditation. A student tutor must be identified truthfully; platform approval does not mean they are a qualified teacher, hold SACE registration or have passed every possible background check. No promise of income, teaching-practice credit or employment is made. The company remains responsible for its own service promises and duties; describing tutors as independent does not remove them.

## Account closure and service changes
You may request closure and cancellation of future services through support. Resolve existing bookings and explain how any unused prepaid entitlement will be treated. Closure, cancellation of renewal and personal-data erasure are separate requests; none removes a lawful refund or payment obligation. We must not use closure to confiscate earned sums or lawful consumer remedies.

Non-urgent account termination requires appropriate notice and an opportunity to respond or remedy the issue where required. A serious safety, fraud or security risk can justify immediate protective restriction while a human reviews the matter. Request review through support. Material paid features must not be removed without the notice, alternative performance or refund required by law.

## Content licence and complaints about content
You keep ownership of your original materials. You give us a non-exclusive licence only as needed to host, format, display and deliver the material to its intended audience for the service. This does not give us unrestricted permission to use a child's work or likeness in advertising. Tell support about suspected copyright infringement with the relevant link, your rights and the basis of your report. We may restrict disputed content while reviewing; legal reporting and response rights remain.

## Complaints and notices
Send service, safety, privacy and contract notices to aneleq@techandguard.co.za; use "Safeguarding" for a safety report and "Privacy — Information Officer" for a privacy request. Include a reference, facts and requested remedy; do not send passwords or full payment credentials. We aim to acknowledge ordinary complaints within two business days and provide a response or progress update within ten business days. These are service targets, not a restriction on earlier statutory remedies. Safety reports are prioritised, but the inbox is not an emergency service or guaranteed to be monitored continuously.

You may approach the Information Regulator for data-protection matters, the National Consumer Commission or an applicable consumer forum, and a competent court as permitted by law. No mandatory private arbitration, shortened statutory deadline or internal-review prerequisite is imposed. South African law applies. These terms do not establish any unverified accreditation or a guarantee of legal compliance.

# Student Terms and Conditions

## Student responsibilities
Use your own account for learning, respect classmates and tutors, and provide an accurate grade and subject selection. A parent or competent guardian must authorise a minor's participation where required. Keep personal details out of public study posts. Obtain help if anyone asks for money outside approved payment channels, private images or unsafe contact.

## Learning and tutoring
Resources and quizzes support learning; results are not official school marks. Verify important information with your teacher. A verified tutor listing is not a guarantee of outcomes or a blanket safeguarding certification. Attend the booked session on time with suitable internet/device access. Do not record a tutor or another participant without valid permission. Arrange guardian supervision appropriate to your circumstances.

## Payments and cancellations
Read the shared subscription and booking policy before paying. Subscription charges normally pay for the access period and platform operating costs; mandatory refund rights are preserved. A paid tutoring booking cancelled at least 24 hours before the session is eligible for a full booking-fee refund. Use the in-app cancellation action and provide a written message to the tutor so they can rearrange their day. Keep the cancellation reference. Do not rely only on closing the browser or an unrelated chat message. If the app is unavailable, contact support with the booking reference and ask for recorded notice to the tutor; a technical failure must not erase your legal rights.

## Safety, privacy and complaints
Report bullying, inappropriate materials or tutor misconduct. Learner-approved parent links control routine progress sharing; guardian-authority questions receive separate review. Ask support for a secure process to submit a completed guardian/indemnity form or request access/deletion. Do not post completed forms in study rooms. The general Terms of Service, Privacy Notice and shared refund policy apply; no provision removes statutory rights.

## Safe use and getting help
Keep contact in the agreed learning channels. You may stop a lesson or conversation that makes you feel unsafe and tell a trusted adult and support. Do not agree to secret meetings, intimate images, threats, gifts with conditions or instructions to hide contact from a guardian. Report misconduct even if you previously agreed to speak to the person. Reporting a genuine concern does not itself justify punishment or loss of a valid refund.

Study resources and AI must support your own learning. Do not submit another person's work as yours, impersonate an examiner or distribute restricted examination material. Do not publish another learner's marks, messages or identity. Ask for help if a feature or policy is unclear.

## Agreement and records
A minor's own checkbox or signature does not substitute for legally required competent-person authorisation. Accepting participation risks does not waive legal protection. A learner aged 18 or older can make their own decisions subject to applicable law. Requests for correction, deletion, account closure or complaints go to support; the main notice explains identity checks and lawful retention.

# Tutor Policies, Terms and Conditions

## Accurate professional profile
Provide accurate qualifications, institution/SACE details where applicable, subject competence, availability and rates. Keep your bio and introduction truthful. Only publish media you own or have permission to use. Explicitly acknowledge that profile media is public. Never upload a learner's likeness, clearance document or confidential credential as a public introduction. Approval is subject to continuing review and is not an employment appointment or a guarantee of income.

## Sessions and safeguarding
Confirm bookings only when you can deliver. Be punctual, prepare suitable material and maintain professional boundaries, especially with minors. No sexual, discriminatory, threatening or exploitative conduct; no requests for private images or unauthorised personal information. Keep communications within the agreed platform channels. Obtain valid consent before recording, retain only necessary records, and report safeguarding concerns through appropriate channels.

## Cancellation and settlement
A student's paid booking cancellation at least 24 hours before the scheduled session is eligible for full repayment of the booking fee. Read the written cancellation notice and acknowledge receipt where possible so you can re-plan your day. If you cancel or fail to provide the booked service, the learner must not fund a service you did not supply; a paid booking is referred for full refund. Late cancellations and exceptional circumstances require fair review, not automatic forfeiture irrespective of law. Do not pressure a learner to waive mandatory rights.

Tutor payouts are separate from subscription revenue and may only use confirmed payment records. The disclosed commission/flat-fee agreement controls permitted deductions; deductions may not be invented retrospectively. Settlement must account for completion, genuine disputes, chargebacks and refund obligations before release. Payment tools are not active merely because this document describes them. Before you accept a paid booking, the company must provide and agree a private commercial schedule stating the gross rate, commission/flat fees, permitted deductions, payout cycle, method and dispute procedure. If these terms are missing or the payment process is unavailable, do not accept the booking as a confirmed paid engagement.

## Account conduct and liability
Do not redirect platform customers to evade agreed fees, misrepresent authority, misuse learner data or infringe materials. A proportionate contractual claim for losses caused by your proven breach or unlawful conduct may apply, subject to lawful process; no unlimited automatic penalty is imposed. Fraud, wilful misconduct and gross negligence cannot be shielded by an indemnity. A classification clause alone does not determine employment status in law. The general service terms, privacy notice and refund policy apply.

## Eligibility and safeguarding checks
Applicants must be adults and must accurately identify themselves as a university student tutor or a qualified/professional tutor as applicable. Do not imply that platform approval confers a teaching qualification or SACE registration. Supply evidence privately when requested; approval is limited to the checks actually performed. Where a role requires registration or legally required suitability screening, that requirement must be met before the activity. No document here substitutes for screening.

Do not communicate sexually with a learner, seek a private/intimate image, arrange a secret meeting, use corporal punishment, discriminate or exploit financial need. Do not promise secrecy about abuse. A guardian's consent cannot authorise abusive or unlawful conduct. Do not record or use learner media without separate lawful permissions. Protect passwords, restrict access to your device and report suspected data exposure.

## Teaching and availability
Keep availability current and decline work you cannot deliver competently. Agree lesson scope and delivery arrangements in the booking record; communicate changes promptly. Do not mark a session complete before delivery or manufacture attendance/feedback. Report disputed completion and preserve relevant records privately. This platform experience is not automatically recognised university teaching practice.

## Finance and end of engagement
The company must disclose changes to future commercial terms before you accept affected work. Already agreed earnings must not be reduced retrospectively. Any hold related to a genuine refund/dispute must be explained, limited to the amount reasonably at issue and reviewed; unrelated undisputed earnings must not be withheld as punishment. Do not collect learners' card details or promise earnings before payment and service conditions are met. Applicable tax and employment duties are determined by the facts and law, not merely this contract's label.

You may stop offering future availability by notifying support and removing it, while fairly resolving confirmed bookings. Suspension or removal follows the safety/fair-review process in the general terms. Confidentiality and legitimate outstanding financial duties continue. You can request review through support without forfeiting accrued legal rights.

title: Child Safeguarding, Conduct and Complaints Policy
content:
# Child Safeguarding, Conduct and Complaints Policy

SmartBridge FET | TECH AND GUARD (Pty) Ltd
Version 2.0 | Effective 17 October 2026

## 1. Purpose and contact
Learner safety applies to administrators, tutors, parents and users. Report concerns privately to [aneleq@techandguard.co.za](mailto:aneleq@techandguard.co.za), with "Safeguarding" in the subject. This is not an emergency response service and continuous monitoring is not promised. If a person is in immediate danger, seek urgent help from the relevant emergency services or police and a trusted adult; do not wait for an app response.

## 2. Preventive duties
The company must check tutor identity, declared qualifications/status and suitability for the proposed activities, including any legally required register/background checks, before allowing the relevant child-facing work. An application approval or profile badge must not imply checks that were never performed. Student tutors must not be presented as qualified teachers unless they are. Guardian authority must be established before relying on guardian consent; an unverified email link is insufficient.

Use agreed teaching channels, appropriate material and age-appropriate supervision. Any in-person arrangement needs separate safety and location arrangements with the competent person; a generic online booking is not approval of an unsupervised home visit. Learners may leave a session that feels unsafe and report the reason.

## 3. Prohibited conduct
Sexual or romantic approaches to learners, grooming, intimate-image requests, threats, discrimination, humiliation, corporal punishment, coercion, exploitation, secret meetings and demands to conceal contact are prohibited. No one may buy a child's silence, pressure a learner to withdraw a report or retaliate for a good-faith complaint. General consent never authorises abuse. Tutors must not use learner contact details for private marketing or share confidential records with unrelated people.

## 4. Media, recordings and information
Do not record sessions or publish learner names, faces, voices, marks or testimonials without an appropriate lawful basis and specific permissions. Core participation consent does not provide those permissions. Never post ID documents, completed forms, payment details or allegations in public study areas. Use proportionate private evidence collection; do not circulate suspected illegal images or ask a child to resend them.

## 5. Receiving a report
Provide the account/session reference, a factual description, approximate time and the safest way to contact you. Share only necessary evidence through a private route arranged with support. Listen calmly, avoid leading questions, do not blame the learner and do not promise absolute secrecy. Explain that information may need to reach authorised protective services. Staff and tutors must meet any applicable mandatory reporting duties without waiting for an internal investigation.

## 6. Protective response and fair review
On receipt, an authorised administrator must assess immediate risk, restrict relevant access/contact where necessary, preserve limited evidence securely and refer to appropriate authorities where required. Protective suspension is precautionary and is not a finding of guilt. Separate affected users where practicable and explain safe next steps. Handle reports involving an administrator with another authorised reviewer wherever possible.

The respondent should receive enough information and an opportunity to respond where safe and lawful. Protect a child's identity and avoid alerting a person where doing so could increase risk or compromise a lawful investigation. Document reasons, decisions, referrals and review dates. Restrict records to people who need them; no guarantee of total confidentiality is made when disclosure is necessary for protection or law.

## 7. Complaints, outcomes and appeal
Possible outcomes include correction, warning, further checks, access limits, removal, service/refund remedies or referral to a competent authority. Communicate appropriate outcomes without exposing another person's confidential information. Request a human review through support, identifying the decision and reasons challenged. No internal appeal requirement prevents external reporting or legal remedies.

We aim to acknowledge ordinary complaints within two business days and provide a response or progress update within ten business days. Safety reports require priority risk assessment; these targets are not permission to delay an urgent protective action or statutory report. Publication of this policy does not mean screening, training or every operational safeguard has already been completed; those duties require evidence and ongoing work.
